Your sleep target is after midnight, so NESA plans today up to 23:59 and starts tomorrow fresh.
Persistence means a bounded number of meaningful reminders — never an endless stream.

Notifications are turned off for NESA, so reminders cannot be delivered.
Everything NESA needs is granted. The alarm should be dependable.
Android is currently stopping NESA from working reliably in the background. Until these are granted, alarms and reminders may arrive late or not at all.
Allow NESA to run in the background
Without this, Android delays or drops alarms while the phone is idle. This is the single most common reason an alarm does not ring.
Without this, the alarm can drift by several minutes.

Android forbids apps from opening a screen while in the background. This permission is the exemption — without it NESA can only post a notification and hope you tap it, instead of showing the alarm itself.
Android 14 made this a separate permission. Without it the alarm arrives as an ordinary notification instead of taking over the screen.
Without this, NESA cannot show the alarm screen or send reminders.

Some phones — Oppo, Realme, OnePlus, Xiaomi, Huawei and others — add their own "Auto-start" or "Auto-launch" setting that no app can detect or request. If the alarm still does not ring, open NESA in system settings and turn on auto-start, then set battery usage to "Don't optimise" or "Allow background activity".
Alarm is armed in the system
The system is NOT holding an alarm for NESA

Every permission is granted, so the alarm was accepted and then dropped. On Oppo, Realme and OnePlus this happens when the app is swiped out of recent apps. Open recent apps, find NESA, and lock it (the padlock on the app card) so the system stops killing it.
Use your phone\'s own alarm instead

If NESA\'s alarm keeps arriving late on this phone, hand the wake time to the clock app that came with it. That alarm is exempt from the limits NESA is subject to, so it will ring on time.\n\nWhat you give up: the wake challenge does not run, you dismiss it in the clock app, and NESA cannot change or remove it afterwards — Android does not allow that. Change the time here and hand it over again, then delete the old one.
